$comment: The design scale of cmux NEXT webviews: spacing, control heights, icon sizes, radii, the glass levels (chrome, popover, menu, chip: each fixes the tint, the blur radius and saturation and the hairline edge; every web backdrop-filter names one, webviews/scripts/check-glass-levels.ts), the two elevations and the colour roles (leo-workspace design/grid.md, tokens.md, glass.md). webviews/scripts/pages/gen-design-scale.mjs writes the --ds-* block of webviews/src/pages/shared/desktop.css, the Tailwind theme every Tailwind entry imports (webviews/src/ui/theme.generated.css: p-3, rounded-md, text-body, bg-hover, shadow-elevation-2 resolve to these) and the TypeScript list the gallery's token sheet renders (webviews/src/ui/designTokens.generated.ts). It also reads schemas/type-scale/type-scale.json and schemas/motion-scale/motion-scale.json for the type and motion utilities. Colour roles are never literals: each names the variable the host derives from the active terminal theme (WebTheme.swift, theme/appTheme.ts), with a system-colour fallback for a page with no host yet. `bun run check:design-scale` fails when a copy drifts.

spacing.$comment: Tailwind's spacing unit is the grid base (--grid-base, 4 px times the interface scale): p-1 is 4, p-3 is 12, gap-6 is 24. The named steps are the scale tokens.md names.

controls.name: row
controls.for: compact rows, menu rows, default buttons

icons.for: status marks, chevrons, spinners, close marks, dots
menu row icons and marks inline with text

radii.name: sm
radii.for: a row highlight inside a 4 px inset

namedRadii.name: control
namedRadii.for: every button: the tab's corner (Metrics.buttonCornerRadius; Lawrence 2026-11-12, buttons round as tabs)

namedRadii.name: card
namedRadii.for: today's card radius; grid.md moves it to 12 after a gallery comparison

namedRadii.name: composer
namedRadii.for: today's composer radius; grid.md moves it to 12 after a gallery comparison

glass.name: chrome
glass.for: chrome docked on the window where no native glass is under the page: panes, bars, rails, side tabs, sticky headers and the minimap; over the App's own window glass the page draws text only (design/glass-system.md, rule 1)

glass.name: popover
glass.for: glass in the page that floats but is not a popup: the composer, Session Info, the running tray, side tabs and viewers (artTint over art or a see-through window)

glass.name: menu
glass.for: every floating popup, menu, picker and card, web and native (design/surface-materials.md, One floating material); veil is the theme surface the page or the App lays on the App's own glass under it (Swift GlassMenuMaterial reads the same numbers)

glass.name: chip
glass.for: small glass on one line: tooltips, the find pill and chips; the tint is the host's contrast-fitted --cmux-tooltip-tint (TooltipSurface.swift), this percentage of the popup surface before the host speaks; the blur and the floor are the native tooltip's (TooltipSurface.blurRadius, minimumTintAlpha)

glass.name: lens
glass.for: a mode, not a level: while the lens draws the wallpaper behind the glass, every level takes this tint and frost

glass.name: fisheye
glass.for: a mode, not a level: the Jump to latest fisheye (design/glass.md): the bend stays, the frost runs after it

glassSaturation.for: the one saturation every glass level frosts with (design/glass-system.md, rule 3); the lens and fisheye modes keep their own

glassEdge.for: the one edge of plain glass (design/glass-system.md, rule 4): the host's hairline ring (--glass-edge, the card rim) plus a lit top hairline, the light's share of --cmux-tone-light on each side

glassContent.for: a card in the content layer (.ui-glass-content: a permission ask, a turn error, a Settings card): the theme surface at this share with no backdrop-filter, since it scrolls with the content; near-solid, under the glass rule's 90% cap, so a wallpaper behind a see-through page shows only faintly (design/glass-system.md, rule 2)

glassInk.for: the secondary ink on glass (design/glass-system.md, rule 5): the theme's text at this share over the glass, so a hint, a placeholder or a detail line keeps 3:1 over the glass laid on pure black, pure white and a busy wallpaper at every floating level, without raising the tint; every glass surface's secondary tokens (--cmux-text-secondary, --agent-muted, the composer placeholder) read it while glass draws; status is the share of a status hue (red, amber, green) in a status word on glass, the rest the theme's text, so the word keeps 3:1 under dark glass on a white page (the page's hues are fitted to the opaque page)

glassUnderlay.for: the theme surface a floating glass lays under its tint in a see-through Chromium page where the page cannot blur itself: the menu's 80% over 40% covers 88%, not 93% (design/glass-system.md, rule 6)

glassMaterial.for: the neutral glass every neutral overlay role is one of (FloatingGlassStyle.look; schemas/surface-roles): the gray its veil mixes at the role's opacity on each side, and the lit and shaded rims, so the sidebar's cards, group headers and sheets are one material with only their opacities apart

transientMaterial.for: One regular translucent material for non-chat popovers, menus, tooltips, palettes, toasts and sheets; native system menus retain their system material

elevation.for: popovers, menus, the palette, hover cards, the composer, sheets and find bars

surfaces.for: The content surface levels of a page (design/chat-surfaces.md; Lawrence 2026-11-19: "bgs are different, we need to make all bgs consistent, from first principles"). A content surface sits on the page, which is opaque in an opaque window and clear over the window's glass, wallpaper or custom background, so a level is never the page colour, black, white or a glass veil: it is the page's ink (the text colour, --ds-surface-ink) laid over clear at a fixed share. Ink over clear keeps the same step against whatever is under it, flips with light and dark on its own, and lets the art show through. A level nested in another adds its step again, so its step to its parent never changes. Floating surfaces are glass (the glass levels), never these; states are the colour roles hover, pressed and selection.

levels.name: card
levels.for: a container of content in the page: the transcript's tool, edit, error and permission cards, plans, code blocks, tool output, the subagent card

levels.name: inset
levels.for: a piece inside a card or inline in text: an icon tile, inline code, a chip, a key cap, a filled secondary control

levels.name: hover
levels.for: a control in the page under the pointer: half way from clear to pressed, so it shows over glass and a picture as over an opaque page (the host's chrome hover, ink 4% in light, read ΔL* 2 over a wallpaper)

levels.name: control
levels.for: the outline of a secondary button at rest; its hover and press take the hover and pressed roles

colors.name: surface
colors.for: the page and pane surface, opaque

colors.name: elevated
colors.for: menus, popovers and sheets under Reduce Transparency

colors.name: faint
colors.for: tertiary text, placeholders and quiet glyphs

colors.name: pressed
colors.fallback: light-dark(color-mix(in srgb, var(--cmux-text, CanvasText) 11%, transparent), color-mix(in srgb, var(--cmux-text, CanvasText) 14%, transparent))
colors.for: a control while pressed: the text over clear (pressedFill 11% light, 14% dark), never the app theme's opaque pressed surface, so a press stays a wash on glass and over a picture

colors.name: selection
colors.for: a selected row or the checked segment

colors.name: separator
colors.for: hairlines inside a page: list rows, cards and fields

colors.name: divider
colors.for: a page's chrome line against the window chrome (WebTheme: the separator x the divider strength, the window's sidebar line and split lines); an older app's sidebar line, else the separator

colors.name: focus
colors.for: the keyboard focus ring (desktop.css: the host's ring at 48%)

colors.name: accent
colors.for: the theme accent: the text colour unless the theme names a hue

colors.name: on-accent
colors.for: text and glyphs on the accent
